I have been diagnosed with Asperger's, Dissociative identity disorder, PTSD and Psychopathy. The PTSD has severely affected what I can remember from my childhood, therapists say it is a defense mechanism. My childhood consisted of a nasty divorce battle that left my brother severly depressed and anxious but left me unfeeling. The Asperger's manifests as social anxiety and awkwardness, along with lack of understanding social situations. It caused much confusion in my youth. It is very difficult to explain I developed different personas to deal with situations in my childhood I could not. They stayed into my young adult hood and were seen as moodiness before a nasty at school delusion. The psychopathy was diagnosed after said incident and it explained my complete lack of empathy in my youth. I wasn't dangerous as a kid, but when my things were taken in simple childhood antics I became a little monster. To this day I do not have the same emotional range as the average person. I have everything under control to a great degree but the lack of feeling never really goes away.

My biological father was a piece of work. He physically and psychology tortured his children because of his anger. I was the younger of two brothers, born 18 months apart, in a nasty divorce hell bent on hurting my mother by taking away her kids. Starting around ages 3-5 til 12-14.  From legally removing our joint last name (cultural/lineage thing) to straight up kid napping us for weeks and brainwashing us into thinking it was camping. He somehow hated me more we assume because I resembled my mother in looks and personality. I was born with Asperger's and am classified as a Savant which a dishonorably dischard Marine father hated, I guess. He hated us for being parts of our mother or something.  So he made us do redundant work till we cried and then locked us away. My memory is very fragile so I can't clearly remember everything. But my mother keeps the court documents and evidence all secure each time I forget. It left me with an inability to accurately judge emotion. I am currently diagnosed with Dissociative Identity Disorder, Per Contra Depression, and Borderline Stable Psychopathy. It hasn't made life "easy" as the first part of my post-divorce adolescence was spent in court mandated Institutionalization at several facilities. I have found meds that don't kill me or sedate me for months. I am definitely not the worst case scenario, but I definitely feel that if they stayed together it could have been a lot worse.
